hypotheses.justification: The theorem also takes `[DecidableEq ι]`. Without the subtype binder, `Function.update z i c` in the statement still elaborates: instance search finds Mathlib's/core's `Subtype` decidable-equality instance, built from `DecidableEq ι`. Nothing else uses the binder. The statement stays true because `Function.update` gives the same value whichever `DecidableEq` instance it uses, since `Decidable` is a subsingleton. The identity holds for every choice of instance, including the derived one. The proof still works. `domDomRestrict_aux` takes an arbitrary `[DecidableEq {a // P a}]`, and with the predicate `fun a => ¬ P a` its instance argument is filled by the derived subtype instance. That is the same instance the statement now uses, so `simpa only [dite_not] using domDomRestrict_aux _ z (fun j ↦ x ⟨j.1, not_not.mp j.2⟩) i c` goes through unchanged. Proving it directly by `grind`, the way `domDomRestrict_aux` itself is proved, should also work. `[DecidableEq ι]` cannot be removed instead: the update on the right-hand side is over `ι` and needs it, and no other hypothesis supplies it.
